question: Amit wants to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that he can contest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amit wants to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India.
 
• He can contest elections in** two constituencies.**
 
• If a candidate is contesting from more than one constituency, he has to lodge a separate return of election expenses for every election which he has contested.
 
• The maximum limits of** election expenditure vary from State to State.**
 
• The lowest limit at present for a parliamentary constituency is:
 
 
• **Rs. 16 lakhs for the constituency of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu and Lakshadweep.**
 
 
 
• The lowest limit for assembly constituency is:
 
 
• **Rs. 8 lakh in **Manipur, **Goa, Meghalaya, **Nagaland, **Mizoram, Sikkim, Tripura and Puducherry.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• On January 25, 1950, the **Election Commission of India** was constituted in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• Election Commission of India:
 
 
• The Election Commission of India is a permanent and autonomous body constituted by the Indian Constitution to ensure free and fair elections.
 
• The Constitution of India (Article 324) has vested in the Election Commission of India the superintendence, direction, and control of the entire process for conduct of elections to Parliament and Legislature of every State and the offices of President and Vice-President of India.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, the Election Commission of India (ECI) is a self-governing constitutional body that regulates the election process in India.
 
• There are currently** two Election Commissioners and a Chief Election Commissioner.**
